text_en: Again, one preparing to sail and about to voyage over raging waves calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the ship that carries him.
text_cn: 再如：有个准备航海的人，行将在怒涛中航行之际，竟向一块比自己乘的船还易坏的木头呼求。

text_en: For it was desire for gain that planned that vessel, and wisdom was the artisan who built it;
text_cn: 船固然是因求财的贪心而发明的，亦是匠人以智慧造成的；

text_en: but it is your providence, O Father, that steers its course, because you have given it a path in the sea, and a safe way through the waves,
text_cn: 但最后，父啊！还是你的照顾在驾驶，因为原是你在海洋中划出了一条路线，在波浪中开辟了一条安全的路径，

text_en: showing that you can save from every danger, so that even a person who lacks skill may put to sea.
text_cn: 表示你能救人脱离各种危险，连没有技术的人，也能航海。

text_en: It is your will that works of your wisdom should not be without effect; therefore people trust their lives even to the smallest piece of wood, and passing through the billows on a raft they come safely to land.
text_cn: 你决不愿使你智慧的工作弃之不用，因此，人将生命托给一片小木，藉一叶扁舟，经过巨涛而平安到达海岸。

text_en: For even in the beginning, when arrogant giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft, and guided by your hand left to the world the seed of a new generation.
text_cn: 其实，在当初，当那些傲慢的巨人被灭绝的时候，世界的希望逃入了一叶扁舟，经你手的驾驶，才得给后世留下了新生的苗裔。

text_en: For blessed is the wood by which righteousness comes.
text_cn: 木头如使用得当，是可祝福的；

text_en: But the idol made with hands is accursed, and so is the one who made it— he for having made it, and the perishable thing because it was named a god.
text_cn: 但是，人手造的木偶和木偶的制造者，却是可诅咒的：制造者，因为他造了木偶；木偶，因为虽是腐败的东西，竟被称为神。

text_en: For equally hateful to God are the ungodly and their ungodliness;
text_cn: 不虔敬的人，与他行的不虔敬的事，同样为天主所憎恶；

text_en: for what was done will be punished together with the one who did it.
text_cn: 所以，木偶与造木偶的，都必遭受惩罚。

text_en: Therefore there will be a visitation also upon the heathen idols, because, though part of what God created, they became an abomination, snares for human souls and a trap for the feet of the foolish.
text_cn: 为此，天主必要惩罚列邦的偶像，因为偶像在天主的造物中，成了可憎之物， 成了人们灵魂的障碍，作了愚人脚前的陷阱。

text_en: For the idea of making idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them was the corruption of life;
text_cn: 发明偶像，是淫乱的开端；创造偶像，是人生的腐败。

text_en: for they did not exist from the beginning, nor will they last forever.
text_cn: 起初原无偶像，也不能永久长存；

text_en: For through human vanity they entered the world, and therefore their speedy end has been planned.
text_cn: 由于人的虚荣心，偶像才进入了世界；为此，已注定很快就要结束。

text_en: For a father, consumed with grief at an untimely bereavement, made an image of his child, who had been suddenly taken from him; he now honored as a god what was once a dead human being, and handed on to his dependents secret rites and initiations.
text_cn: 一个父亲因他儿子的夭折，甚为悲伤，遂为自己早死的儿子立像，他虽是已死的人，如今却敬之如神，并传令家属礼拜献祭。

text_en: Then the ungodly custom, grown strong with time, was kept as a law, and at the command of monarchs carved images were worshiped.
text_cn: 这种不虔敬的事，相沿日久，便成了习俗，以致守如法律；再加上君王的命令，雕像遂受崇拜。

text_en: When people could not honor monarchs in their presence, since they lived at a distance, they imagined their appearance far away, and made a visible image of the king whom they honored, so that by their zeal they might flatter the absent one as though present.
text_cn: 住在远方的人，不能当面尊敬国王，便由远方设想君王的相貌，为所要尊敬的君王，制造一座可见的肖像，向那不在跟前的，殷勤献媚，如同就在跟前一样。

text_en: Then the ambition of the artisan impelled even those who did not know the king to intensify their worship.
text_cn: 艺术家的野心，把那些不认识君王的人，也都诱来，为扩大这项敬礼；

text_en: For he, perhaps wishing to please his ruler, skillfully forced the likeness to take more beautiful form,
text_cn: 艺术家原为讨有权威者的欢心，就竭力运用自己的技术，使君王的肖像格外美丽；

text_en: and the multitude, attracted by the charm of his work, now regarded as an object of worship the one whom shortly before they had honored as a human being.
text_cn: 民众受了这精美手工的吸引，不久以前那当人尊敬的，现在却奉之为神了。

text_en: And this became a hidden trap for humankind, because people, in bondage to misfortune or to royal authority, bestowed on objects of stone or wood the name that ought not to be shared.
text_cn: 这便成了人生的隐祸，因为遭受不幸，或受暴君压迫的人们，将“那不可道出的名字，”加给了木石。

text_en: Then it was not enough for them to err about the knowledge of God, but though living in great strife due to ignorance, they call such great evils peace.
text_cn: 他们对天主的认识错到如此地步，还以为不足；甚至愚昧使他们生活在强烈的战斗中， 还将这样的大祸，称为和平。

text_en: For whether they kill children in their initiations, or celebrate secret mysteries, or hold frenzied revels with strange customs,
text_cn: 因他们祭杀孩童，或举行秘密祭礼，或仪式怪诞的狂欢宴会。

text_en: they no longer keep either their lives or their marriages pure, but they either treacherously kill one another, or grieve one another by adultery,
text_cn: 谁也不顾及生活与婚姻的纯洁，遂彼此陷害残杀，以奸淫加害于人。

text_en: and all is a raging riot of blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,
text_cn: 于是，混乱到处丛生：流血、杀人、盗窃、欺骗、缺德、失信、暴乱、违约、

text_en: confusion over what is good, forgetfulness of favors, defiling of souls, sexual perversion, disorder in marriages, adultery, and debauchery.
text_cn: 陷害忠良、忘恩负义、玷辱灵魂、同性淫乱、婚姻混杂、通奸淫乱。

text_en: For the worship of idols not to be named is the beginning and cause and end of every evil.
text_cn: 崇拜虚无的偶像，实是万恶的起源、由来和结局。

text_en: For their worshipers either rave in exultation, or prophesy lies, or live unrighteously, or readily commit perjury;
text_cn: 这些人行乐发狂，预言虚妄，生活邪辟，妄发虚誓，

text_en: for because they trust in lifeless idols they swear wicked oaths and expect to suffer no harm.
text_cn: 因为他们信赖无生命的偶像，自以为妄发虚誓，不会受罚。

text_en: But just penalties will overtake them on two counts: because they thought wrongly about God in devoting themselves to idols, and because in deceit they swore unrighteously through contempt for holiness.
text_cn: 但是，正为了这两件事，他们必受公义的处罚：因对天主没有正确的认识，因而崇拜偶像；又因诡计多端，妄发虚誓，因而轻视圣洁。

text_en: For it is not the power of the things by which people swear, but the just penalty for those who sin, that always pursues the transgression of the unrighteous.
text_cn: 因为，那常追击不义者违法行为的，并不是“赖以发誓者”的力量，而是天主对犯罪者的惩罚。
